names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 21 februarie, «Sfântul Mucenic Mavrichie».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 1 Ιουλίου, «Άγιος Μαυρίκιος», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог's heading for 22. фебруар ст. ст., „Свети мученик Маврикије и седамдесет војника.“, with Свети, the rank word мученик and the company clause left off; Apamea, which the folder's English name carries, is in the body.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (19 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 21 februarie — «Sfântul Mucenic Mavrichie»

feast.note: saint.gr's page for this entry carries no life of its own: it prints the distich and then «Βλέπε στις 27 Δεκεμβρίου όπου και η βιογραφία του», sending the reader to its day page for 27 Δεκεμβρίου for the biography. That page has not been read in this wave, so 1 Ιουλίου — the day page actually read — is what is recorded, and whether the Greek calendar's proper day for him is 27 Δεκεμβρίου is a question left open (1 October 2026). The Romanian row keeps him on 21 februarie.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 1ης Ιουλίου — «Άγιος Μαυρίκιος»
Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 07.03.2026 (22. фебруар ст. ст.) — „Свети мученик Маврикије и седамдесет војника.“

attestations.note: The heading names him and the seventy soldiers with him, which is what this folder already holds as one company; the body names one of the seventy, his son Фотин, and no other, so the company is not enumerated and no folder was made for the son.

death.note: The Ohrid Prologue at pravoslavno.rs for the Julian 22 February: „Ови храбри Христови војини пострадаше око 305. године.“ The page says about the year 305, not 305, and it is the only source read for him that gives a year; the folder carried no dates at all before this reading.
